title: The Four-Day Week
intro: More and more companies are testing a shorter working week. Does it really work?

passage: For more than a hundred years, most people in full-time jobs have worked five days a week. The two-day weekend became common in the twentieth century, when factory owners in the United States and Europe decided that rested workers made fewer mistakes. Today, however, a growing number of companies are asking a new question: if people can do the same amount of work in four days, why should they come in for five?

In 2022, one of the largest experiments of this kind took place in the United Kingdom. Around sixty companies, from small restaurants to software firms, took part in a six-month trial. Nearly three thousand employees kept their full salary but worked about 80 per cent of their usual hours. In return, they promised to stay just as productive as before. Researchers from several universities collected information from the workers and their managers before, during and after the trial.

The results surprised many people. Most of the companies said that their income stayed about the same, and some even reported a small increase. Workers took fewer sick days, and many said that they felt less stress and slept better. A large majority of the companies decided to continue with the shorter week after the trial had finished. One manager explained that her team had simply stopped wasting time: meetings became shorter, and people checked their emails less often.

Supporters of the four-day week believe that it can help to reduce some of the biggest problems of modern working life. When people have an extra day off, they can look after children or elderly parents, do exercise or learn new skills. This gives them a better balance between work and home. Companies also hope that a shorter week will help them to attract talented staff, because many young people now say that free time is as important to them as money.

However, the idea does not suit every kind of job. A hospital cannot close on Fridays, and a shop needs staff whenever customers want to buy things. In these workplaces, managers have to create complicated schedules so that someone is always available. Critics also point out that some employees find four longer days tiring, especially if they have to fit five days of tasks into fewer hours. If the pressure becomes too great, the benefits may disappear.

So, is the four-day week the future of work? It is probably too early to say. The trials so far have been fairly short, and most of the companies that joined them were already interested in the idea, which may have affected the results. Even so, the experiments have started an important conversation. Whether or not the five-day week survives, many employers are now thinking more carefully about how efficient their workers are, not just how many hours they spend at their desks.

mcq.q: According to one manager, why did her team manage to do the same work in fewer days?
options: They worked late in the evenings.

mcq.q: What does the writer say about the results of the trials so far?
options: They show that the four-day week works in every job.
They were collected only by the companies themselves.
They may not give us the full picture yet.
